official.description_text:
Researcher in scientific and molecular visualization
Apply for position
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
Job description
PDC is seeking a new member to join its team of research software engineers. The successful candidate will become part of the Scientific Services Group, which is tasked to develop software, and services, enabling research which can streamline data analysis and workflows for scientists at KTH and across Sweden.
In this role, the applicant will be responsible for the development and maintenance of
VIAMD
, a tool for visualizing and interactively analyzing chemistry simulations. Additionally, they will lead collaboration efforts with researchers at the
Wallenberg Wood Science Center (WWSC)
and support molecular dynamics simulations of materials studied at WWSC.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree in scientific molecular visualization.
Advanced experience in software programming languages like C/C++
Long experience in developing 3D graphic applications with tools like OpenGL, OpenCL, CUDA.
Good communication skills with users to inform them of our services.
Good knowledge of the English language, as it is required in day to day work.
Knowledge of diversity and equal treatment issues with a particular focus on gender equality.
Preferred qualifications
The applicant should have good connections with swedish network of users that today make use of swedish supercomputer resources, and within networks focusing on molecular visualization.
We consider it favorable if the applicant has a broad knowledge of programming languages commonly used in this particular area today.
Experience of developing and leading visualization project will be viewed as favorable.
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH
.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system in order to apply for this position. You are responsible to ensure that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Max two pages long.
Your complete application must be received by KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The employment is valid until further notice (permanent post) according to agreement.
The employment begins with a six-month probationary period.
Other information
For

In such cases, a prerequisite for employment is that the applicant is approved following the security clearance.
We firmly decline all contact with staffing and recruitment agencies and job ad salespersons.

ai.summary: Research software engineer position (permanent) in the Scientific Services Group at KTH's PDC centre, focused on developing and maintaining VIAMD visualization software for chemistry simulations and molecular dynamics, plus collaboration with the Wallenberg Wood Science Center.

thematic_fit.rationale: Moderate surface thematic overlap in visualization and 3D interactive systems, but the connection is technical, not human-centred. The core mission is visualization tool development for scientific workflows, not evaluation of human understanding, learning outcomes, or collaborative interaction design. While VIAMD involves interactive visualization, the position is fundamentally a software engineering role for domain scientists, not human-centred HCI research.

methodological_fit.rationale: Partial methodological fit exists in interactive 3D system design and software development (researcher has advanced Unity and C# skills). However, the posting emphasizes graphics rendering (OpenGL, OpenCL, CUDA), which the researcher has not demonstrated proficiency in and which is explicitly listed as an excluded direction (graphics-rendering). The role requires deep systems-level graphics optimization and 3D rendering expertise, not user-centred evaluation or immersive experience design. No user studies, human evaluation, or learning assessment component is mentioned.

growth_value.rationale: Limited growth value. The role would develop graphics programming and 3D visualization skills, which are tangential to—but distinct from—human-centred XR research. The researcher would gain experience maintaining and extending 3D software systems, but would not develop capabilities in experimental design, user research methods, collaborative systems evaluation, or spatial cognition research that align with their target identity. The focus is technical delivery for domain scientists, not research into human interaction or learning.

strategic_value.rationale: Moderate strategic value. KTH is in Sweden (a preferred country), and the position is permanent with stability and international exposure. However, this is a research software engineering role within a computational center, not a doctoral research position within an HCI/XR research group. The supervisor context (Henri Zazzi, PDC Scientific Services) is not documented in relation to human-centred research. While the role offers professional growth and Swedish placement, it does not align with the researcher's target trajectory toward human-centred immersive systems research or doctoral positions in HCI-focused groups.

eligibility_flags: Requires doctoral degree in scientific/molecular visualization or equivalent; researcher's MSc is in Multimedia/HCI with XR focus, not in visualization per se. Equivalence would need to be argued.

Posting demands 'long experience in developing 3D graphic applications with tools like OpenGL, OpenCL, CUDA'—researcher has no documented experience with these graphics APIs. Advanced Unity/C# does not automatically transfer to lower-level graphics work.
Role is permanent and permanent position suggests long-term commitment; alignment with researcher's target identity is weak, raising questions about career sustainability in this track.
risks: Graphics-rendering emphasis (OpenGL, OpenCL, CUDA) aligns with an excluded direction in the researcher's target profile
Role is software engineering focused, not research focused; unlikely to lead naturally toward doctoral research positions in human-centred HCI
Limited user research or human evaluation component; researcher would spend career improving visualization tools for scientists, not researching human interaction or learning in immersive systems
May be perceived as a technical/engineering track rather than a research track, potentially limiting future applications to pure research positions
Researcher's documented graphics skills are not at the level required (would need to self-study OpenGL/CUDA architecture)
